paragraphs: A man had created a lovely garden. One day a cow wandered in and trampled it badly. In a fit of rage he beat the cow, and the blows killed her.
Terrified of the grave sin he had committed, he thought up a clever excuse. Indra is the god who presides over the hand, he reasoned, so surely the hand's deed was Indra's responsibility, not his.

Indra saw through this twisted logic. He came to the garden disguised as a Brahmin and began asking questions. Who planted these trees? Who laid out these paths? Each time, the man proudly replied that he had done it himself.
Then Indra sprang the trap. So you made everything in this garden, he remarked, but only the killing of the cow was Indra's doing?
learn: We love to take credit for our successes and blame circumstances, luck or others for our mistakes. Honest people own both. Taking responsibility for what goes wrong is the first step to growing from it.
